parsed.why: Worst-law group; statewide facilities ban covering restrooms, shelters, dorms and prisons, no statewide GI protections, religious-refusal shield, and court-approved marker denial. Universal-exposure facility risk with no working remedy; below parent.

Most-protective tier: public-accommodations, housing and employment protections covering gender identity, hate-crime enhancements, open state ID rules, repealed sodomy law. Local recourse and no facility ban lift it well above parent, though national border rules remain.

Most-protective tier with shield laws and comprehensive care coverage; facilities not banned. But national border/custody regime persists, prison housing reversal documented, and unresolved anti-trans ballot initiatives temper the gain.

Low-risk group: no bathroom ban, no sex definition, governor vetoed care and sports bans, sodomy repealed. Yet no statewide GI nondiscrimination or hate-crime coverage and restrictive marker rules keep it only modestly above parent.

Worst-law group: school/college bathroom bans, binary-sex statute, felony minor-care ban, surgery-only ID rule upheld by courts, no GI protections or hate-crime coverage. Hostile state layer pushes below parent; violence figure is undercount floor.
